claims.text: Stable oxide-scale formation in CrFeCoNiX alloys is governed by a synergy between interfacial alloy-element diffusion and local metal/oxide interfacial stress.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiAl preferentially forms an Al2O3-containing protective scale.
Al2O3 grows more slowly and is more thermodynamically stable than chromium oxide scales under high-temperature oxidation or corrosion.
Formation of a slowly growing Al2O3 layer minimizes interfacial stress.
CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn forms mixed oxide scales because of mismatched diffusion kinetics.
Mixed oxides in the Si- and Mn-containing variants accumulate greater interfacial stresses that promote cracking or spallation.
Al and Cr form passivating Al2O3 and Cr2O3 oxides in AlCoCrFeNi.
Al diffusion, including grain-boundary diffusion, promotes protective alpha-Al2O3 formation in AlCoCrFeNi.
A balanced interfacial diffusion flux of Al and Cr produces a slowly growing oxide that remains coherent with the metal.
In CrFeCoNiAl, interfacial stress remains below a critical spallation level.
Substitution of Al by Si or Mn disrupts Al/Cr diffusion balance and oxide chemistry.
CrFeCoNiAl will form a scale dominated by Al2O3 with a Cr2O3 contribution during exposure above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit lower interfacial stress and less cracking or spallation than the Si- and Mn-containing variants.
CrFeCoNiMn can form ternary mixed oxides such as Mn3Fe3O8 and MnCr2O4 during high-temperature oxidation.
The Si- and Mn-containing variants will have a greater propensity for oxide-scale cracking or spallation during prolonged exposure.
The proposed comparison uses Si- or Mn-containing alloys as controls with known unstable oxide behavior, high stress accumulation, and rapid oxide degradation.
Alloy chemistry, surface heterogeneity, microstructure, and high-temperature phase instability can produce highly variable oxide structures in high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is restricted to single- or multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions exposed above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.

contradictions.description: The comparison requires substitution among Al, Si, and Mn, so the samples cannot have literally identical compositions as stated in the experimental design. They can instead have identical atomic ratios and processing histories apart from the identity of X.
